note: Re-judged 2026-11-08 (child 22, home-cpe-22 reauth) after responder.go::handleResponderInbound changed in fc9b7f5a3b/f50e28c360/67700fd37e. RFC 3748 Section 4: "Since EAP only defines Codes 1-4, EAP packets with other codes MUST be silently discarded by both authenticators and peers." The only change to handleResponderInbound since the last judgement (9e3ed47790) is the StateEstablished comment, now naming handleHeldSuccessorInbound (held_successor.go); no statement changed and the StateEAPInProgress arm still replays a cached response or reaches handleResponderEAP. The new routing in handleInbound (fsm.go, not a cited unit) calls handleHeldSuccessorInbound first, but holdsSuccessor requires sa.State == StateEstablished, so an SA in StateEAPInProgress always falls through to handleResponderInbound and the EAP discard path is unchanged. fsm.go::handleEAPResponse, responder_eap.go::handleResponderEAP, eap.go::Process and peer.go::Process are byte-identical to the last judgement (the later responder_eap.go and peer.go edits in b0cca10f29 touch eapTLSServerConfig and startTLSClient comments only). The three tagged units are unchanged: TestEngineDiscardedEAPCodesPreserveExchange sends encrypted Codes 0, 5 and 255 into both IKE roles in StateEAPInProgress through handleInbound and asserts state, expected Message ID, last sent message and retransmission state unchanged, then a held-back valid packet at the same Message ID completes both roles with matching nonzero MSKs and a verified AUTH; the core units assert the authenticator answers nothing for Codes 0, 5, 255 and wrong-role Codes, and the peer reports a discard with no response, error, Done or MSK, with state, method and round budget unchanged, before legitimate MS-CHAPv2 packets complete the exchange. Tests not re-run by this judge (read-only phase).
